concept.name: Risk-management error
concept.definition: A breach of the rules that bound loss - oversizing, moving or removing stops, exceeding daily loss limits, adding to losers, or ignoring correlation between positions. It is the most dangerous error class because it converts bounded, survivable mistakes into account-threatening losses.
concept.intuition: You can be wrong a hundred times and survive if risk is controlled; one risk-management error at the wrong leverage can end the account.
concept.mechanics: Measured by comparing realized per-trade and per-day losses and exposures against plan limits and against risk capacity; violations are tagged in the journal and reviewed separately from P&L. Defenses are structural: hard stops, platform-enforced size and loss limits, and sizing formulas tied to invalidation distance.
concept.failure_modes: These errors cluster during tilt and after losses, when the urge to recover overrides limits; they are also hidden by luck - oversized bets that win teach the wrong lesson until variance collects. Correlated positions make nominal diversification illusory.
concept.misconceptions: Risk management is not a drag on returns bolted onto the strategy; sizing and exits are part of the strategy's expectancy. A stop that was never hit by luck does not prove the oversize was safe.
concept.example: Plan caps risk at 0.5% per trade and 1.5% per day; during a news spike the trader doubles size and lifts the stop, taking a 4% hit - logged in review as a risk-management error, the category the plan exists to prevent.
